newsitem.title: USA: Temple-Inland to buy California Financial.
newsitem.headline: Temple-Inland to buy California Financial.

text.p: Temple-Inland Inc. said Monday it will acquire California Financial Holding Co., another California-based banking company, for $30 a share, or about $150 million.
Under the definitive agreement, California Federal shareholders can choose to receive Temple-Inland common stock, cash or a combination of the two, the company said.
Temple-Inland, the parent of Guaranty Federal Bank FSB, said it would issue no more than 1.69 million common shares in the deal.
Guaranty Federal operates 113 banking centres in Texas with over $9 billion in assets and $6.3 billion in deposits.
California Financial is the parent of Stockton Savings Bank FSB in Stockton, Calif., with about $1.3 billion in assets and 23 branches in the Central Valley of California.
The deal is expected to close in the second quarter of 1997.
Temple-Inland has an option to purchase 940,095 shares, or about 19.9 percent, of California Federal's common stock at $27.25 per share if the deal does not close under certain circumstances.
Temple-Inland, based in Diboll, Texas, is a major manufacturer of paper, corrugated packaging and building products, with financial services operations in mortgage and consumer banking.
California Federal's stock edged down 6.25 cents to $28.9375 on Nasdaq at midday. Temple-Inland rose 12.5 cents to $54.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
